hazards.reason: Copying customer holds the database's write lock for time that grows with the table.
hazards.subject: table/customer

hazards.reason: SQLite's ALTER TABLE cannot change the default of referrer_id, so the step rebuilds customer: it copies the rows into a new table, drops the old one and renames the new one, with foreign keys off.
hazards.subject: table/customer

statements:
CREATE TABLE "_new_customer" (
  "id" TEXT DEFAULT (lower(hex(randomblob(4)) || '-' || hex(randomblob(2)) || '-4' || substr(hex(randomblob(2)), 2) || '-' || substr('89ab', 1 + (random() & 3), 1) || substr(hex(randomblob(2)), 2) || '-' || hex(randomblob(6)))) NOT NULL,
  "name" TEXT NOT NULL,
  "email" TEXT COLLATE NOCASE NOT NULL,
  "created_at" TEXT DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now')) NOT NULL,
  "referrer_id" TEXT DEFAULT (lower(hex(randomblob(4)) || '-' || hex(randomblob(2)) || '-4' || substr(hex(randomblob(2)), 2) || '-' || substr('89ab', 1 + (random() & 3), 1) || substr(hex(randomblob(2)), 2) || '-' || hex(randomblob(6)))),
  PRIMARY KEY ("id")
)
steps.subject: table/customer
